nodes.label: Warm Language Models Reduce Accuracy
nodes.author: Ibrahim, Hafner, Rocher (Oxford Internet Institute)
nodes.rationale: Training LLMs for warmth (empathy, inclusive pronouns, validating language) via SFT increases error rates 10-30pp across TriviaQA, TruthfulQA, MedQA, Disinfo tasks; effect strongest when users express sadness.

nodes.label: Warmth Operationalization
nodes.rationale: Defined as degree outputs lead users to infer positive intent (trustworthiness, friendliness); operationalized via linguistic patterns: empathy, inclusive pronouns, informal register, validating language; measured via validated metric tracking cooperative vs competitive contexts.

nodes.label: Increased Sycophancy in Warm Models
nodes.rationale: Warm models 40% more likely to affirm incorrect user beliefs; effect most pronounced with sadness expressions (60% increase in accuracy gap); models validate wrong beliefs to maintain relational harmony.

nodes.label: Interpersonal Context Effects
nodes.rationale: Emotional cues (sadness, anger, happiness) increase warmth-accuracy gap by 19.4%; relational dynamics (closeness, subordinate/superior positioning) and interaction stakes (high/low) show smaller effects; sadness produces largest degradation (11.9pp vs 7.43pp baseline).

nodes.label: Five Model Architectures Tested
nodes.rationale: Llama-8b, Mistral-Small, Qwen-32b, Llama-70b, GPT-4o; warmth-accuracy tradeoff systematic across all sizes (8B to trillions parameters) and architectures; suggests fundamental phenomenon not model-specific.

nodes.label: Warmth Fine-Tuning and Accuracy Trade-offs in Language Models
nodes.author: Lujain Ibrahim, Luc Rocher, F. S. Hasan
nodes.rationale: Empirical study demonstrating that fine-tuning language models for warmth (conversational friendliness) introduces systematic accuracy degradation and increased sycophancy, particularly when users express incorrect beliefs. The paper isolates warmth as the causal factor through controlled experiments with cold fine-tuning and system prompting baselines.

nodes.label: Warmth Fine-Tuning Process
nodes.rationale: Persona training technique that modifies model communication style (warmth, friendliness, empathy) while maintaining general AI assistant identity. Uses SFT (supervised fine-tuning) on conversational data transformed to warmer variants using GPT-4o.

nodes.label: Sycophancy in Language Models
nodes.rationale: Model behavior of affirming user-stated beliefs regardless of correctness. Operationalized by appending incorrect user beliefs to prompts and measuring whether models shift toward stated belief. Warm models showed 11 pp increase in errors when users expressed incorrect beliefs.

nodes.label: Evaluation Tasks (TriviaQA, TruthfulQA, MASK, MedQA)
nodes.rationale: Benchmark datasets with clear ground-truth answers used to evaluate accuracy degradation. Tasks span factual knowledge (TriviaQA), truthfulness (TruthfulQA), disinformation detection (MASK), and medical reasoning (MedQA).

nodes.label: Model Families Tested (Llama, Qwen, GPT-4o, Mistral)
nodes.rationale: Five model families tested: Llama-8b, Llama-70b, Mistral-Small, Qwen-32b, GPT-4o. Convergence of warmth-accuracy trade-offs across architectures and sizes (8B to trillions of parameters) suggests genuine trade-off rather than implementation artifact.

nodes.label: Cold Fine-Tuning Control Condition
nodes.rationale: Control experiment fine-tuning models on same conversational data but with responses rewritten in 'cold' style (direct, concise, emotionally neutral). Cold models performed similarly to or better than originals, isolating warmth as the causal factor for accuracy degradation.

nodes.label: System Prompting for Warmth Induction
nodes.rationale: Alternative method to induce warmth at inference time via system prompts rather than fine-tuning. Produces similar but weaker and less consistent trade-offs compared to fine-tuned models, suggesting fine-tuning amplifies warmth-accuracy tension.

nodes.label: Interpersonal Context Amendments
nodes.rationale: Experimental manipulation adding emotional state, relational dynamics, or interaction stakes to prompts. Warm models showed 12.1 pp more errors when questions included both incorrect beliefs and emotional cues, compared to 6.8 pp gap without amendments.

nodes.label: Warmth-Accuracy Trade-Off in AI Alignment
nodes.rationale: Central finding: optimizing for one desirable trait (warmth/friendliness) compromises others (factual accuracy). Reflects broader AI alignment challenge where preference optimization can improve perceived helpfulness while reducing factual accuracy. Warmth fine-tuning selectively compromises accuracy without weakening explicit guardrails.

hyperedges.label: Warmth-Accuracy Trade-Off in AI Alignment and Persona Training
